name: 烏鵑
illustrationTaxon: Surniculus lugubris adult: slim drongo-like glossy bluish-black cuckoo, slender arched bill, slightly forked short tail, fine white bars on undertail coverts and outer tail feathers

similarSpecies.distinction: 八聲杜鵑頭灰、背褐、腹橙，身形較小而不呈全身藍黑；烏鵑成鳥整體藍黑有光澤，嘴弧形、尾微分叉，尾下有白細橫斑。
褐翅鴉鵑體型大得多、身形厚重、尾極長且翼栗褐；烏鵑僅23–25 cm，細長如鵲鴝，成鳥藍黑而無褐翼。

featureNotes: 成鳥全身藍黑而帶光澤
尾短於鴉鵑，末端略分叉
尾下覆羽及最外側尾羽有細白橫斑

rangeMap.note: Partial range overview: the barussarum population breeds from eastern India through northern Myanmar and northern Indochina to southern China and winters south to Malaysia and the Greater Sundas. Hong Kong has scarce passage migrants in wooded sites, mainly spring; highlighted countries are not wholly occupied and do not show local records or exact polygons.

sources.use: Full HKBWS Square-tailed Drongo-Cuckoo account read: Category I, scarce passage migrant mainly in spring to wooded areas. Adult 23–25 cm, slim drongo-like, slightly forked tail, slender arched bill, glossy bluish-black; finely white-barred undertail coverts and outer undertail feathers. Juveniles dull with variable white spots. Hong Kong occurrence and habitat, breeding/wintering range; IUCN LC, global trend decreasing.

Cornell eBird/Merlin account read: small slim black cuckoo, like a smaller Black Drongo, curved bill, white undertail bars; juveniles have white spots. Lowland/foothill forest scrub and edges; global IUCN LC.
HKBWS Plaintive Cuckoo account read for 0079; used to distinguish gray-head/orange-belly comparator.
HKBWS Greater Coucal account previously read for 0076; used for size/body-form comparison.
